newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares climb to new record, not over yet.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares climb to new record, not over yet.

text.p: Danish share prices surged on to a new record closing high on Friday, buoyed by a strong dollar and USA and dealers saw more advances early next week.

"It looked for a while like we might see the KFX slip, but the U.S. non-farm payroll data for January triggered a recovery. We should see more advances on Monday echoing the booming American market," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index rose 0.66 point to 152.90, the seventh consecutive end-of-day record high in overall bourse turnover of 1.456 billion crowns. The KFX March future rose 0.65 point to 151.60 with 385 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Banks were in focus again, rallying from earlier losses. Den Danske Bank finished two crowns higher at 569, while rival Unidanmark shed seven crowns to close at 355.
The day's clear winners were Novo Nordisk, which put on 15 crowns to end the week at the highest level so far this year of 600 crowns and Sophus Berendsen, which climbed 12 crowns to 875.
